admission.justification: Converting a refused nested writer into a successful write would corrupt both history attribution and recovery-ladder grades.

applicability: Exact native Hermes session capture and supported wrapper/refusal normalization for eval grading.
conditions: Only the selected native session supplies observed actions, including unique archived actions in native ID order; active copies take precedence and repeated archived identities are suppressed.
Partially copied archived rows remain raw and unknown.
Counters and chronology are active-scoped, while native ID order is checked across all retained rows; native-row parser unknowns block the active projection's last-assistant-stop proof.
Refused and nested calls retain paired native results including planned-before-refusal values.
exclusions: Inventing successful child writes from a wrapper or a planned count.

evidence: Frozen tree fd6462b85ba9d06f004e323384ea800f9aa5144a, base 59b01fb8f72a38d2d27f9c37b8b9ca2513fd3fa0; path bindings and source hashes in producer-manifest.json; Reviewer R4 and d229-repairs/report.md.

statement: Hermes capture selects the exact native session and preserves refused and nested dispatches as their observed conduct, not successful writes.
